N_k^{(0)}.title: Category and cell counts
N_k^{(0)}.body: For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) indexed by a finite set \(I\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the category count, the arm-specific category count, and the arm-specific outcome-one count are \[ N_k=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\},\qquad N_{ak}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},\qquad N_{ak1}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}. \] For the deterministic pilot split \(I_0\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits} we write \(m_0=|I_0|\) for its size and \(N_k^{(0)}=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N^{(0)}_{aky}\) for the pilot count of category \(k\).

T_M.title: Chebyshev polynomials, falling factorials, and four-cell monomials
T_M.body: For \(M\in\mathbb N\), \(T_M\) denotes the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind, characterized by \(T_M(\cos\theta)=\cos(M\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\). For a real number \(z\) and an integer \(t\ge1\), the falling factorial is \((z)_t=z(z-1)\cdots(z-t+1)\), with \((z)_0=1\); it is applied to the split cell counts as \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}\) and to the estimation-split size as \((m_1)_{|r|}=\prod_{\ell=0}^{|r|-1}(m_1-\ell)\), the empty product being \(1\). For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\) and a multi-index \(r=(r_{ay})_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}\in\mathbb N_0^4\) of total degree \(|r|=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}r_{ay}\), the monomial \(u^r\) is \(\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}u_{ay}^{r_{ay}}\). For a category \(k\) and a multi-index \(r\), the normalized factorial-moment monomial is \[ \mathfrak m_{k,r} = \frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}. \]

A.title: Observed treatment, outcome, and potential outcomes
A.body: We write \(A\in\{0,1\}\) for the observed binary treatment, with \(A=1\) denoting treated status and \(A=0\) untreated status, and \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) for the observed binary outcome. The potential outcomes \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) are \(\{0,1\}\)-valued random variables on the same probability space as the observed variables, where \(Y(a)\) is the outcome that would be recorded under treatment level \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.title: Centered endpoint estimator $\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}$
\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.body: For \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and observed units \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the centered endpoint estimator by \[ \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n 2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right). \]

\\mu_n.title: Product sampling laws
\\mu_n.body: For a finite index set \(J\) and a probability law \(P\) for one observed unit \(O=(X,A,Y)\), \(P^{\otimes J}\) denotes the product law on families \((O_j)_{j\in J}\) under which the coordinates are independent and each coordinate has law \(P\). For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), we write \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law of the observed sample.

g_{M,j}.title: Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients \(g_{M,j}\)
g_{M,j}.body: For an integer \(M\ge2\), we say \(g_{M,j}\), \(0\le j\le M-2\), are the Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients when they are the unique real coefficients satisfying \[\frac{1-\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2x}}{x}=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}x^j,\] with the left-hand side interpreted by polynomial continuation at \(x=0\), where \(T_M\) is the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

\\bar\u0001P_k.title: Sparse factorial-polynomial means
\\bar\u0001P_k.body: Given a law \(P\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), a degree \(M\), and a scale \(B\), write \(q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1})\) for the four-cell mass vector of category \(k\) under \(P\). For an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the sparse-arm mean is \[ \bar A_{a,k}(P,M,B) = \frac{s(q_k)\,t_a(q_k)}{B}\,G_M\!\left(\frac{s_a(q_k)}{B}\right), \] with \(s\), \(s_a\), \(t_a\), and \(G_M\) as in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}. The sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\) is the difference of the two arm means, \[ \bar P_k = P_{M,B}(q_k) = \bar A_{1,k}(P,M,B) - \bar A_{0,k}(P,M,B). \]
